I have been working this land for 40 years. I know every corner of my 8 mu. My husband and I, just the two of us now, we do the main work ourselves. I do not need to think too hard about what to plant — it is always wheat then maize, same as my parents did, same as everyone in Quzhou does.

**Wheat (October planting):** I will plant the whole 8 mu in wheat after the maize comes off. I buy improved seed from the village supply shop — Jimai variety, the kind my neighbors use and that I have had good results with. For fertilizer, I put down compound fertilizer as base before planting, then come spring I spread urea when the wheat starts jointing. I irrigate four times: once before winter to help the roots set, once at jointing, once at heading, once during grain filling. My well handles it fine. I spray twice — once for weeds in winter, once for aphids and rust in spring. I use rotary tillage after maize harvest to break up the stubble before I sow.

**Maize (June planting):** Right after wheat harvest, I plant maize — hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whatever the shop has. I use rotary tillage lightly to work in the stubble, then plant. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea at the big bell stage. I water three times: once to get germination going if it is dry, once at tasseling, once at grain fill. I spray herbicide early, then treat for corn borer once. By late September it is ready.

I do not try new things at my age. What I do feeds us and earns a little. That is enough.
